- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.33) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.25) in recent days, model underestimates; adjust upward, especially if price is trending down.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in the 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days), especially after price spikes; apply downward bias to first 5 days.
- After a price spike (e.g., >70.5), model often overshoots in the next 3–5 days; cap forecast at +10% above spike peak or use moving average of prior 5 days.
- Mean reversion is strong in 10–15 day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 5–10%.
- If sentiment is flat (0.00) and price is trending, model often fails to capture momentum; use 3-day moving average of true price for smoothing.
- Model underestimates in 20–30 day horizon when sentiment is neutral or slightly positive; add 2–5% bias to end of forecast.
